https://github.com/sktime/sktime/pull/11.headline: Forecasts past the training data crashed
https://github.com/sktime/sktime/pull/11.problem: After statsmodels 0.15, sktime's ARIMA and AutoARIMA forecasters failed when asked to predict beyond the training data on index types statsmodels doesn't support.
https://github.com/sktime/sktime/pull/11.approach: Fixed the out-of-sample prediction path so those indices are handled again and the forecast comes back on the original index.

https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/.headline: Two builds, one version number
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/.problem: PyTorch builds its own Triton wheels, and they carried the same version as upstream Triton, so the two were easy to mix up on the download server (issue #195141).
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/.approach: Investigated PyTorch issue #195141 (Triton download server) and opened a PR proposing a fix; maintainers resolved it through a test-infra workflow.

https://github.com/data-privacy-stack/pr.headline: The type checker rejected the quickstart
https://github.com/data-privacy-stack/pr.problem: Running mypy --strict on Presidio's analyze → anonymize quickstart reported errors: the anonymizer engines' constructor was untyped, and a list of PatternRecognizer was rejected where a list of EntityRecognizer was expected (issue #1396).
https://github.com/data-privacy-stack/pr.approach: Opened a PR that adds a return type to EngineBase.__init__ and widens ad_hoc_recognizers from List to Sequence. It cuts the quickstart's mypy errors from 3 to 1 with no runtime change; the last one is handled by a separate redesign (#2414).
